ticket.title: TypeError when saving a product with a supplier ID returned as string
ticket.bug:
When PDO returns numeric database values as strings, saving a product with an associated supplier can trigger a `TypeError`:

```text
PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Core\Domain\Supplier\ValueObject\SupplierId::__construct():
Argument #1 ($supplierId) must be of type int, string given

called in:
src/Core/Domain/Product/Supplier/Command/SetSuppliersCommand.php
```

The issue occurs while supplier IDs are processed by `SetSuppliersCommand`.

Depending on the PDO/database environment, a supplier ID can be returned as a numeric string, for example `"1"`, while `SupplierId` expects an `int`.

This is another occurrence of the numeric-string type issue tracked in #38735.

A similar occurrence was reported in #42447 and is handled separately by #42475 for the product grid and product pack flows.
ticket.steps:
The problem can be reproduced by forcing PDO to return fetched numeric values as strings.

Temporarily modify `classes/db/DbPDO.php` in the `getPDO()` method.

Replace:

```php
return new PDO(
    $dsn,
    $user,
    $password,
    $options
);
```

with:

```php
$pdo = new PDO(
    $dsn,
    $user,
    $password,
    $options
);

$pdo->setAttribute(PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES, true);

return $pdo;
```

This modification is only required to reproduce the affected PDO behavior and must not be committed.

Then:

1. Make sure at least one supplier exists.
2. Associate the supplier with a product.
3. Go to **BO > Catalog > Products**.
4. Edit the product.
5. Make any editable change.
6. Save the product.
7. Verify that a `TypeError` is triggered in `SupplierId::__construct()` because the supplier ID is provided as a string.

After the test, revert the temporary change to `classes/db/DbPDO.php`.

resolution.title: Fix supplier ID type in SetSuppliersCommand
resolution.description: Fixes a `TypeError` when supplier IDs are provided as numeric strings to `SetSuppliersCommand`. Supplier IDs are now explicitly normalized to integers before creating `SupplierId` value objects. |
resolution.how_to_test: See below 👇 |
resolution.author: Codencode

ticket.title: `actionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore` variables are overwritten in `FrontController::assignGeneralPurposeVariables()`
ticket.bug:
There is a regression in `FrontController::assignGeneralPurposeVariables()` affecting the `actionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore` hook.

This hook receives `$templateVars` by reference and is intended to allow modules to define or override template variables before the core assigns its general-purpose variables.

However, after the hook is executed, `$templateVars` is completely reassigned:

```php
$templateVars = [
    'cart' => $this->cart_presenter->present($cart, true),
    'currency' => $this->getTemplateVarCurrency(),
    'customer' => $this->getTemplateVarCustomer(),
    'country' => $this->objectPresenter->present($this->context->country),
    'language' => $this->objectPresenter->present($this->context->language),
    'page' => $this->getTemplateVarPage(),
    'shop' => $this->getTemplateVarShop(),
    'core_js_public_path' => $this->getCoreJsPublicPath(),
    'urls' => $this->getTemplateVarUrls(),
    'configuration' => $this->getTemplateVarConfiguration(),
    'field_required' => $this->context->customer->validateFieldsRequiredDatabase(),
    'breadcrumb' => $this->getBreadcrumb(),
    'link' => $this->context->link,
    'time' => time(),
    'static_token' => Tools::getToken(false),
    'token' => Tools::getToken(),
    'debug' => _PS_MODE_DEV_,
];
```

As a consequence, any variable added by a module through `actionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore` is lost.

For example:

```php
public function hookActionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore(array $params): void
{
    $params['templateVars']['test_variable'] = 'test value';
}
```

`test_variable` is no longer available in Smarty after the hook execution.

This appears to be a regression from the previous implementation, where core variables were assigned individually using the existing value when already provided:

```php
$templateVars['cart'] = $templateVars['cart'] ?? $this->cart_presenter->present($cart);
```

That implementation preserved variables added by modules and also allowed modules to provide a value before the core calculated it.
ticket.expected:
Variables added to `$templateVars` from `actionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore` should still be available in Smarty after `assignGeneralPurposeVariables()` has completed.

For example:

```php
$params['templateVars']['test_variable'] = 'test value';
```

should make the following usable from a Smarty template:

```smarty
{$test_variable}
```

Existing core variables provided by the hook should also not be overwritten, consistently with the previous behavior of this hook.
ticket.steps:
1. Install the [issueactionfrontcontrollersetvariablesbefore.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31307869/issueactionfrontcontrollersetvariablesbefore.zip) module.
2. Go to the Front Office.
3. In the footer, you should see the value value. Instead, **Variable not set** is displayed, indicating that the variable added by the module is not available in the template.

resolution.title: Fix #42395: Prevent template variables from being overwritten
resolution.description: This PR fixes a regression affecting the `actionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore` and `action{ControllerName}SetVariablesBefore` hooks. Variables added to `$templateVars` through these hooks were lost because `$templateVars` was completely reassigned afterwards in `FrontController::assignGeneralPurposeVariables()`. The fix preserves the variables already defined by the hooks while still assigning the default Front Office template variables.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Install the [issueactionfrontcontrollersetvariablesbefore.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31308081/issueactionfrontcontrollersetvariablesbefore.zip) test module. 2. Go to the Front Office. 3. Check the footer. 4. Before this fix, `Variable not set` is displayed. 5. After this fix, the expected value `value` is displayed.
resolution.author: Codencode

ticket.title: Order confirmation email ignores the order state's "Attach invoice PDF to email" checkbox setting
ticket.bug:
Order confirmation email attaches the invoice PDF based on the order state's `invoice` flag instead of `pdf_invoice`. That meeans that unchecking **"Attach invoice PDF to email"** on an order status is silently ignored for the order confirmation email, as long as that status has the *Invoice* toggle  enabled.

The result is that on order confirmation, the customer gets an invoice attachment even if that option is explicitly disabled in the order state's configuration
ticket.expected:
No invoice attachment in email since the **Attach PDF to email** is unchecked
The `order_conf` attachment should honour `pdf_invoice`, consistent with the field's help text ("This will attach invoice PDF to the sent email, if it exists. If it doesn't, it will have no effect.")
ticket.steps:
1. Go to **Shop Parameters > Order Settings > Statuses**.
2. Pick the status your payment method validates orders into (e.g. *Processing* or *Payment accepted*), and make sure the invoice toggle is on.
3. Edit the said order state, and **uncheck "Attach invoice PDF to email"**. 
4. Place an order through that payment method on the front office.

ticket.title: Pack stock type "Decrement pack only" is ignored by Pack::getQuantity() - empty() treats STOCK_TYPE_PACK_ONLY (0) as "Default"
ticket.bug:
A pack whose per-product stock behavior is explicitly set to **"Decrement pack only"** (`pack_stock_type = 0`, `PackStockType::STOCK_TYPE_PACK_ONLY`) is treated as if it was set to "Default" by `Pack::getQuantity()`, so its displayed/available quantity is resolved using the **global** `PS_PACK_STOCK_TYPE` configuration instead of the pack's own setting.

**Root cause** - `classes/Pack.php`, `Pack::getQuantity()`:

https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/classes/Pack.php#L293

```php
// If no pack stock or shop default, set it from configuration
if (empty($packStockType) || $packStockType == self::STOCK_TYPE_DEFAULT) {
    $packStockType = Configuration::get('PS_PACK_STOCK_TYPE');
}
```

`STOCK_TYPE_PACK_ONLY === 0` and `empty(0) === true`, so an explicit "Decrement pack only" is indistinguishable from "not set" and always falls back to the global configuration. The per-pack value 0 only "works" when the global default happens to be "Decrement pack only" as well. Values 1 ("products only"), 2 ("both") and 3 ("default") behave correctly.

The same line is present in all maintained branches:
- `develop`: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/classes/Pack.php#L293
- `8.2.x`: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/8.2.x/classes/Pack.php#L311
- `9.0.0`: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/9.0.0/classes/Pack.php#L313

**Why this is more than a display glitch** - the stock *decrement* path uses exact comparisons and DOES honor the per-pack value 0 (`StockManager::updatePackQuantity()`):

https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/src/Core/Stock/StockManager.php#L45-L70

So for a pack set to "Decrement pack only" while the shop default is "Decrement products in pack only" (or "both"):
- placing an order decrements the **pack's own** stock (per-pack setting honored),
- but the FO product page, listings, and availability checks (`Product::getQuantity()` → `Pack::getQuantity()`, `Pack::isInStock()`) display a quantity computed **from the pack's components** (per-pack setting ignored, global used).

The displayed availability is therefore computed from stock that is never decremented by sales of this pack, and the two numbers drift apart with every order. Since `Pack::isInStock()` relies on the same method, cart availability checks use the wrong mode as well - this may be (part of) the root cause of the overselling symptoms reported in #26728.

**Suggested fix** - stop treating the legitimate value 0 as "unset", while keeping the legacy NULL/empty-string fallback that `empty()` presumably guarded:

```php
if ($packStockType === null || $packStockType === '' || (int) $packStockType == self::STOCK_TYPE_DEFAULT) {
    $packStockType = Configuration::get('PS_PACK_STOCK_TYPE');
}
```

**Related:** #26728 (open symptom report: overselling with "Decrement pack only" / "Decrement both"), #19846 (pack stock EPIC), PR #35372 (last refactor of this method, 8.1.5 - the `empty()` condition was kept unchanged).
ticket.expected: The pack's available quantity should be **1** - its own stock - because the pack explicitly overrides the shop default with "Decrement pack only". Ordering the pack decrements the pack's own stock, consistently with what is displayed.
ticket.steps:
1. Fresh PrestaShop install (reproduced on 8.1.7; the affected code is identical on `8.2.x`, `9.0.0` and `develop`), stock management enabled.
2. In BO: Shop Parameters > Product Settings > set **"Default pack stock management"** to **"Decrement products in pack only"**.
3. Create standard product A with quantity **10** and standard product B with quantity **20**.
4. Create a pack containing **2 × A** and **1 × B**. Set the pack's own quantity to **1** and set the pack's stock management option (product page > Quantities) to **"Decrement pack only"**.
5. Open the pack's product page in the front office (or call `Product::getQuantity($idPack)` / check the displayed availability).
6. (Divergence part) Place an order for 1 pack and compare which stock was decremented vs. which stock the FO displays.

resolution.title: Fix Pack::getQuantity ignoring 'Decrement pack only' stock type
resolution.description: Pack::getQuantity() resolved the pack stock type with empty($packStockType), which treats the legitimate value 0 (PackStockType::STOCK_TYPE_PACK_ONLY, "Decrement pack only") as unset and falls back to the global PS_PACK_STOCK_TYPE configuration. Displayed pack availability was therefore computed with the wrong mode, while the stock decrement path (StockManager::updatePackQuantity()) honors the per-pack setting, so the displayed stock and the actually decremented stock diverge with every order. This PR replaces empty() with explicit null / empty-string checks so an explicit "Decrement pack only" is honored, while keeping the legacy fallback for NULL values from old databases. |
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Shop Parameters > Product Settings > set "Default pack stock management" to "Decrement products in pack only". 2. Create product A (qty 10) and product B (qty 20). 3. Create a pack containing 2×A + 1×B, set the pack's own quantity to 1 and its stock management (product page > Quantities) to "Decrement pack only". 4. Open the pack's page in FO. Before this fix the displayed quantity is 5 (computed from components per the global setting); after the fix it is 1 (the pack's own stock — per-pack setting honored). |
resolution.author: samilmarekrygula

ticket.title: Product combination field unit_price_impact can't be update
ticket.bug:
When I try to update the Unit Price Impact (Excluding Tax) field of one product combination, the display appears to have saved my changes. However, when I check the front end, the unit price has not been changed.
In the database tables (ps_product_attribute and ps_product_attribute_shop), the unit_price_impact field has not been changed.
ticket.expected: The Unit Price Impact of my product combination should have changed and this should be visible in FO with the unit price when I change the product combination.
ticket.steps:
1. Go to the a product with combination in BO
2. In tab Price, activate Price unite (by entering the unit sales price (excluding VAT) and the unity)
3. In tab Combination, select at least one combination and click to bulk edit
4. In the Price section, enter the price for the field Impact on unit price (excluding VAT)
5. Check in FO if the display unit price change for the concerned combination (and unit_price_impact in database)

resolution.title: Fix bulk combination edit not saving the unit price impact
resolution.description: When bulk editing combinations (select combinations → bulk edit → Price section), the **Impact on price per unit (tax excl.)** field appeared to save but never persisted: `unit_price_impact` stayed unchanged in `product_attribute` and the front office unit price did not change. The bulk form submits this field as `[price][unit_price]` and `BulkCombinationFormDataFormatter` remapped it to `[price_impact][unit_price]`, but the combination command builder reads the unit price impact from `[price_impact][unit_price_tax_excluded]` (mapped to `setImpactOnUnitPrice`). The value therefore landed at a path nothing consumed and was silently dropped, while all the other bulk price fields (which map to matching paths) saved correctly. The fix remaps the bulk field to `[price_impact][unit_price_tax_excluded]`.
resolution.how_to_test: On a product with combinations, set a unit price + unity in the Price tab. In the Combinations tab, select one or more combinations, use bulk edit, and set "Impact on price per unit (tax excl.)". Before: `product_attribute.unit_price_impact` stays unchanged and the FO unit price is unaffected. After: the impact is saved and reflected in the FO. Covered by the updated `tests/Unit/Core/Form/IdentifiableObject/DataFormatter/BulkCombinationFormDataFormatterTest.php` (the bulk field now formats to `[price_impact][unit_price_tax_excluded]`).
resolution.author: boo-code

ticket.title: BO - Tax rules - Exception thrown when trying to delete a country linked to the tax rule
ticket.bug: `AdminTaxRulesGroupControllerCore::deleteTaxRule(): Argument #1 ($id_tax_rule_list) must be of type array, bool given, called in /controllers/admin/AdminTaxRulesGroupController.php on line 510` Not a regression, in PS 1.7.8.8 : PS : Works well with normal deletion, issue is just with bulk action
ticket.steps:
1. Go to BO > International > Taxes > Tax rules
2. Edit any tax rule
3. Click Bulk Action > Select All > Delete selected
4. Add a new tax rule with one country > Save and stay
5. See error

resolution.title: Fix TypeError on tax rules bulk delete when no rule is selected
resolution.description: `AdminTaxRulesGroupController::processBulkDeleteTaxRules()` passed `Tools::getValue('tax_ruleBox')` straight into `deleteTaxRule(array $id_tax_rule_list)`. When the bulk **Delete** action on the tax rules of a tax rules group is triggered with no row checked, `tax_ruleBox` is absent from the request and `Tools::getValue()` returns `false`, throwing `AdminTaxRulesGroupControllerCore::deleteTaxRule(): Argument #1 ($id_tax_rule_list) must be of type array, bool given`. The fix bails out early when nothing is selected (there is nothing to delete), which both removes the `TypeError` and avoids redirecting with a misleading "successful deletion" confirmation for an empty selection.
resolution.how_to_test: BO > International > Taxes > Tax Rules > edit a tax rules group. Use the rows' Bulk actions > Delete with **no** row selected (the report also reaches it after deleting all rules then re-saving). Before: a `TypeError` is thrown. After: the action is a no-op (nothing selected, nothing deleted). Covered by `tests/Integration/Classes/AdminTaxRulesGroupBulkDeleteTest.php` (fails on the base branch with the exact `TypeError`, passes with the fix).
resolution.author: boo-code

ticket.title: TypeError when saving a product with a supplier ID returned as string
ticket.bug:
When PDO returns numeric database values as strings, saving a product with an associated supplier can trigger a `TypeError`:

```text
PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Core\Domain\Supplier\ValueObject\SupplierId::__construct():
Argument #1 ($supplierId) must be of type int, string given

called in:
src/Core/Domain/Product/Supplier/Command/SetSuppliersCommand.php
```

The issue occurs while supplier IDs are processed by `SetSuppliersCommand`.

Depending on the PDO/database environment, a supplier ID can be returned as a numeric string, for example `"1"`, while `SupplierId` expects an `int`.

This is another occurrence of the numeric-string type issue tracked in #38735.

A similar occurrence was reported in #42447 and is handled separately by #42475 for the product grid and product pack flows.
ticket.steps:
The problem can be reproduced by forcing PDO to return fetched numeric values as strings.

Temporarily modify `classes/db/DbPDO.php` in the `getPDO()` method.

Replace:

```php
return new PDO(
    $dsn,
    $user,
    $password,
    $options
);
```

with:

```php
$pdo = new PDO(
    $dsn,
    $user,
    $password,
    $options
);

$pdo->setAttribute(PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES, true);

return $pdo;
```

This modification is only required to reproduce the affected PDO behavior and must not be committed.

Then:

1. Make sure at least one supplier exists.
2. Associate the supplier with a product.
3. Go to **BO > Catalog > Products**.
4. Edit the product.
5. Make any editable change.
6. Save the product.
7. Verify that a `TypeError` is triggered in `SupplierId::__construct()` because the supplier ID is provided as a string.

After the test, revert the temporary change to `classes/db/DbPDO.php`.

resolution.title: Fix supplier ID type in SetSuppliersCommand
resolution.description: Fixes a `TypeError` when supplier IDs are provided as numeric strings to `SetSuppliersCommand`. Supplier IDs are now explicitly normalized to integers before creating `SupplierId` value objects. |
resolution.how_to_test: See below 👇 |
resolution.author: Codencode

ticket.title: `actionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore` variables are overwritten in `FrontController::assignGeneralPurposeVariables()`
ticket.bug:
There is a regression in `FrontController::assignGeneralPurposeVariables()` affecting the `actionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore` hook.

This hook receives `$templateVars` by reference and is intended to allow modules to define or override template variables before the core assigns its general-purpose variables.

However, after the hook is executed, `$templateVars` is completely reassigned:

```php
$templateVars = [
    'cart' => $this->cart_presenter->present($cart, true),
    'currency' => $this->getTemplateVarCurrency(),
    'customer' => $this->getTemplateVarCustomer(),
    'country' => $this->objectPresenter->present($this->context->country),
    'language' => $this->objectPresenter->present($this->context->language),
    'page' => $this->getTemplateVarPage(),
    'shop' => $this->getTemplateVarShop(),
    'core_js_public_path' => $this->getCoreJsPublicPath(),
    'urls' => $this->getTemplateVarUrls(),
    'configuration' => $this->getTemplateVarConfiguration(),
    'field_required' => $this->context->customer->validateFieldsRequiredDatabase(),
    'breadcrumb' => $this->getBreadcrumb(),
    'link' => $this->context->link,
    'time' => time(),
    'static_token' => Tools::getToken(false),
    'token' => Tools::getToken(),
    'debug' => _PS_MODE_DEV_,
];
```

As a consequence, any variable added by a module through `actionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore` is lost.

For example:

```php
public function hookActionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore(array $params): void
{
    $params['templateVars']['test_variable'] = 'test value';
}
```

`test_variable` is no longer available in Smarty after the hook execution.

This appears to be a regression from the previous implementation, where core variables were assigned individually using the existing value when already provided:

```php
$templateVars['cart'] = $templateVars['cart'] ?? $this->cart_presenter->present($cart);
```

That implementation preserved variables added by modules and also allowed modules to provide a value before the core calculated it.
ticket.expected:
Variables added to `$templateVars` from `actionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore` should still be available in Smarty after `assignGeneralPurposeVariables()` has completed.

For example:

```php
$params['templateVars']['test_variable'] = 'test value';
```

should make the following usable from a Smarty template:

```smarty
{$test_variable}
```

Existing core variables provided by the hook should also not be overwritten, consistently with the previous behavior of this hook.
ticket.steps:
1. Install the [issueactionfrontcontrollersetvariablesbefore.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31307869/issueactionfrontcontrollersetvariablesbefore.zip) module.
2. Go to the Front Office.
3. In the footer, you should see the value value. Instead, **Variable not set** is displayed, indicating that the variable added by the module is not available in the template.

resolution.title: Fix #42395: Prevent template variables from being overwritten
resolution.description: This PR fixes a regression affecting the `actionFrontControllerSetVariablesBefore` and `action{ControllerName}SetVariablesBefore` hooks. Variables added to `$templateVars` through these hooks were lost because `$templateVars` was completely reassigned afterwards in `FrontController::assignGeneralPurposeVariables()`. The fix preserves the variables already defined by the hooks while still assigning the default Front Office template variables.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Install the [issueactionfrontcontrollersetvariablesbefore.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31308081/issueactionfrontcontrollersetvariablesbefore.zip) test module. 2. Go to the Front Office. 3. Check the footer. 4. Before this fix, `Variable not set` is displayed. 5. After this fix, the expected value `value` is displayed.
resolution.author: Codencode

ticket.title: Pack stock type "Decrement pack only" is ignored by Pack::getQuantity() - empty() treats STOCK_TYPE_PACK_ONLY (0) as "Default"
ticket.bug:
A pack whose per-product stock behavior is explicitly set to **"Decrement pack only"** (`pack_stock_type = 0`, `PackStockType::STOCK_TYPE_PACK_ONLY`) is treated as if it was set to "Default" by `Pack::getQuantity()`, so its displayed/available quantity is resolved using the **global** `PS_PACK_STOCK_TYPE` configuration instead of the pack's own setting.

**Root cause** - `classes/Pack.php`, `Pack::getQuantity()`:

https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/classes/Pack.php#L293

```php
// If no pack stock or shop default, set it from configuration
if (empty($packStockType) || $packStockType == self::STOCK_TYPE_DEFAULT) {
    $packStockType = Configuration::get('PS_PACK_STOCK_TYPE');
}
```

`STOCK_TYPE_PACK_ONLY === 0` and `empty(0) === true`, so an explicit "Decrement pack only" is indistinguishable from "not set" and always falls back to the global configuration. The per-pack value 0 only "works" when the global default happens to be "Decrement pack only" as well. Values 1 ("products only"), 2 ("both") and 3 ("default") behave correctly.

The same line is present in all maintained branches:
- `develop`: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/classes/Pack.php#L293
- `8.2.x`: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/8.2.x/classes/Pack.php#L311
- `9.0.0`: https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/9.0.0/classes/Pack.php#L313

**Why this is more than a display glitch** - the stock *decrement* path uses exact comparisons and DOES honor the per-pack value 0 (`StockManager::updatePackQuantity()`):

https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/develop/src/Core/Stock/StockManager.php#L45-L70

So for a pack set to "Decrement pack only" while the shop default is "Decrement products in pack only" (or "both"):
- placing an order decrements the **pack's own** stock (per-pack setting honored),
- but the FO product page, listings, and availability checks (`Product::getQuantity()` → `Pack::getQuantity()`, `Pack::isInStock()`) display a quantity computed **from the pack's components** (per-pack setting ignored, global used).

The displayed availability is therefore computed from stock that is never decremented by sales of this pack, and the two numbers drift apart with every order. Since `Pack::isInStock()` relies on the same method, cart availability checks use the wrong mode as well - this may be (part of) the root cause of the overselling symptoms reported in #26728.

**Suggested fix** - stop treating the legitimate value 0 as "unset", while keeping the legacy NULL/empty-string fallback that `empty()` presumably guarded:

```php
if ($packStockType === null || $packStockType === '' || (int) $packStockType == self::STOCK_TYPE_DEFAULT) {
    $packStockType = Configuration::get('PS_PACK_STOCK_TYPE');
}
```

**Related:** #26728 (open symptom report: overselling with "Decrement pack only" / "Decrement both"), #19846 (pack stock EPIC), PR #35372 (last refactor of this method, 8.1.5 - the `empty()` condition was kept unchanged).
ticket.expected: The pack's available quantity should be **1** - its own stock - because the pack explicitly overrides the shop default with "Decrement pack only". Ordering the pack decrements the pack's own stock, consistently with what is displayed.
ticket.steps:
1. Fresh PrestaShop install (reproduced on 8.1.7; the affected code is identical on `8.2.x`, `9.0.0` and `develop`), stock management enabled.
2. In BO: Shop Parameters > Product Settings > set **"Default pack stock management"** to **"Decrement products in pack only"**.
3. Create standard product A with quantity **10** and standard product B with quantity **20**.
4. Create a pack containing **2 × A** and **1 × B**. Set the pack's own quantity to **1** and set the pack's stock management option (product page > Quantities) to **"Decrement pack only"**.
5. Open the pack's product page in the front office (or call `Product::getQuantity($idPack)` / check the displayed availability).
6. (Divergence part) Place an order for 1 pack and compare which stock was decremented vs. which stock the FO displays.

resolution.title: Fix Pack::getQuantity ignoring 'Decrement pack only' stock type
resolution.description: Pack::getQuantity() resolved the pack stock type with empty($packStockType), which treats the legitimate value 0 (PackStockType::STOCK_TYPE_PACK_ONLY, "Decrement pack only") as unset and falls back to the global PS_PACK_STOCK_TYPE configuration. Displayed pack availability was therefore computed with the wrong mode, while the stock decrement path (StockManager::updatePackQuantity()) honors the per-pack setting, so the displayed stock and the actually decremented stock diverge with every order. This PR replaces empty() with explicit null / empty-string checks so an explicit "Decrement pack only" is honored, while keeping the legacy fallback for NULL values from old databases. |
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Shop Parameters > Product Settings > set "Default pack stock management" to "Decrement products in pack only". 2. Create product A (qty 10) and product B (qty 20). 3. Create a pack containing 2×A + 1×B, set the pack's own quantity to 1 and its stock management (product page > Quantities) to "Decrement pack only". 4. Open the pack's page in FO. Before this fix the displayed quantity is 5 (computed from components per the global setting); after the fix it is 1 (the pack's own stock — per-pack setting honored). |
resolution.author: samilmarekrygula

resolution.title: Fix bulk combination edit not saving the unit price impact
resolution.description: When bulk editing combinations (select combinations → bulk edit → Price section), the **Impact on price per unit (tax excl.)** field appeared to save but never persisted: `unit_price_impact` stayed unchanged in `product_attribute` and the front office unit price did not change. The bulk form submits this field as `[price][unit_price]` and `BulkCombinationFormDataFormatter` remapped it to `[price_impact][unit_price]`, but the combination command builder reads the unit price impact from `[price_impact][unit_price_tax_excluded]` (mapped to `setImpactOnUnitPrice`). The value therefore landed at a path nothing consumed and was silently dropped, while all the other bulk price fields (which map to matching paths) saved correctly. The fix remaps the bulk field to `[price_impact][unit_price_tax_excluded]`.
resolution.how_to_test: On a product with combinations, set a unit price + unity in the Price tab. In the Combinations tab, select one or more combinations, use bulk edit, and set "Impact on price per unit (tax excl.)". Before: `product_attribute.unit_price_impact` stays unchanged and the FO unit price is unaffected. After: the impact is saved and reflected in the FO. Covered by the updated `tests/Unit/Core/Form/IdentifiableObject/DataFormatter/BulkCombinationFormDataFormatterTest.php` (the bulk field now formats to `[price_impact][unit_price_tax_excluded]`).
resolution.author: boo-code

ticket.title: BO - Tax rules - Exception thrown when trying to delete a country linked to the tax rule
ticket.bug: `AdminTaxRulesGroupControllerCore::deleteTaxRule(): Argument #1 ($id_tax_rule_list) must be of type array, bool given, called in /controllers/admin/AdminTaxRulesGroupController.php on line 510` Not a regression, in PS 1.7.8.8 : PS : Works well with normal deletion, issue is just with bulk action
ticket.steps:
1. Go to BO > International > Taxes > Tax rules
2. Edit any tax rule
3. Click Bulk Action > Select All > Delete selected
4. Add a new tax rule with one country > Save and stay
5. See error

resolution.title: Fix TypeError on tax rules bulk delete when no rule is selected
resolution.description: `AdminTaxRulesGroupController::processBulkDeleteTaxRules()` passed `Tools::getValue('tax_ruleBox')` straight into `deleteTaxRule(array $id_tax_rule_list)`. When the bulk **Delete** action on the tax rules of a tax rules group is triggered with no row checked, `tax_ruleBox` is absent from the request and `Tools::getValue()` returns `false`, throwing `AdminTaxRulesGroupControllerCore::deleteTaxRule(): Argument #1 ($id_tax_rule_list) must be of type array, bool given`. The fix bails out early when nothing is selected (there is nothing to delete), which both removes the `TypeError` and avoids redirecting with a misleading "successful deletion" confirmation for an empty selection.
resolution.how_to_test: BO > International > Taxes > Tax Rules > edit a tax rules group. Use the rows' Bulk actions > Delete with **no** row selected (the report also reaches it after deleting all rules then re-saving). Before: a `TypeError` is thrown. After: the action is a no-op (nothing selected, nothing deleted). Covered by `tests/Integration/Classes/AdminTaxRulesGroupBulkDeleteTest.php` (fails on the base branch with the exact `TypeError`, passes with the fix).
resolution.author: boo-code
